items.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I did Jenny, the betrayer in “Three Penny Opera” with Vanessa Redgrave.

ctx.x: Wow. Well post Lambert, Hendricks & Ross, you did some more theater?

I did some wonderful theater in London. I did “Kennedy’s Children” which is a wonderful play. I did Jenny, the betrayer in “Three Penny Opera” with Vanessa Redgrave. I’ve done all kinds. You know, if I couldn’t work anymore and couldn’t sing anymore, I could always go into the theater and be a wonderful dresser, you know, dress people for their parts. Because I know how to do all that, and stage managing. I’ve had a really good grounding in that. And one is an extension of the other. You know, acting is singing,…
What do you listen to at home these days? Anything in particular?

items.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was a scene where Vanessa and I are in a jeep. We have to go down this road

ctx.x: Okay. Creative writing student. When I see that description – Yanks was one of the early ones. It listed you – in 1979 – listed you as the Red Cross lady.

With Vanessa Redgrave. I don’t drive. I can drive, but not in traffic. So I only drive in movies and t.v. There was a scene where Vanessa and I are in a jeep. We have to go down this road, and we suddenly come across a huge area which is showers, and the guys are naked. Just before John Schlesinger, who’s the director, said, “Action,” Vanessa said to me, “I’m told you don’t drive.” I said, “That’s right” – rrrrrrrrr. We did it, and it was fine. Then John said, “We’re going to have to take another angle.” I said,…
